symbols.name: B^\circ
symbols.def: \(B\) after deleting one redundant observed-cell row for each \(z\in\mathcal Z\)

symbols.name: p_x^\circ
symbols.def: \(p_x\) with the rows matching the deletions in \(B^\circ\)

symbols.name: \widetilde p_x
symbols.role: response-fiber equality right-hand side including normalization

symbols.name: \beta
symbols.space: subsets of \(\mathcal R\) having \(\operatorname{rank}(\widetilde B)\) elements

symbols.name: \mathcal Q^*(P_{\mathrm{obs}})
symbols.role: population correspondence of stratum-specific randomized rules

symbols.name: q_x^*(p_x)
symbols.def: the sole element of \(Q_x^*(p_x)\) whenever that correspondence is a singleton

symbols.name: G_x(p_x)
symbols.def: \(G_{(b,\beta),a}(p_x)=e_b^\top C_\beta\widetilde B_\beta^{-1}\widetilde p_x-e_a^\top C_\beta\widetilde B_\beta^{-1}\widetilde p_x\) for \(b\in\mathcal A\) and \(\beta\in\mathcal B_x(p_x)\)
symbols.role: finite regret-game payoff matrix with observable moving coefficients

symbols.name: \eta_x
symbols.role: simplex-equality multiplier in the active saddle KKT system

symbols.name: \mathcal I_x(p_x)
symbols.def: the regret-scenario rows \(s=(b,\beta)\) carrying positive optimal dual weight \(\lambda_s\)

symbols.name: \mathcal J_x(p_x)
symbols.role: support of the unique population mixture

symbols.name: \mathcal K_j(p_x)
symbols.def: the primal--dual KKT certificate set for \(q=e_j\) in the reduced saddle program

symbols.name: s_a
symbols.def: the spike vector with coordinate \(a\) equal to \(U_{ax}\) and coordinate \(c\neq a\) equal to \(L_{cx}\)

symbols.name: H_x(p_x)
symbols.def: the square active KKT matrix in Definition def:active-system

symbols.name: g_x(p_x)
symbols.role: constant active-system right-hand side on a fixed face

symbols.name: E_x(p_x)
symbols.def: the matrix extracting \(v_x\) and zero-padding the active policy coordinates \(q_{x,\mathcal J_x}^*\) into \(\mathbb R^{K+1}\)

symbols.name: T_x(p_x)
symbols.role: population policy--regret target on a unique face

symbols.name: J_x(p_x)
symbols.role: full policy--value Hadamard derivative with inactive policy coordinates zero-padded

assumptions.condition: \(O_1,\ldots,O_n\) are independent and identically distributed according to \(P_{\mathrm{obs}}\).

standard.name: Uniform nondegeneracy of all basic solutions

assumptions.condition: The reduced saddle program has the singleton primal--dual KKT solution \(\{u_x(p_x)\}\).
\(v_x(p_x)-G_{s,\cdot}(p_x)q_x^*(p_x)\geq\kappa\) for every \(s\notin\mathcal I_x(p_x)\) and every \(x\in\mathcal X\).
\(G_{\cdot,a}(p_x)^\top\lambda-\eta_x\geq\kappa\) for every \(a\notin\mathcal J_x(p_x)\) and every \(x\in\mathcal X\).

standard.name: Uniform strict complementarity of active variables

definitions.name: \mathfrak P_{\mathrm{IV}}
definitions.construction: \(\{P_{\mathrm{obs}}:\text{ Assumptions ass:instrument-randomization, ass:treatment-consistency, ass:outcome-exclusion, ass:stratum-instrument-support, and ass:response-fiber-compatibility hold for every }x\in\mathcal X\}\).

definitions.name: \mathcal W_x(p_x)
definitions.construction: Delete one redundant observed-cell row per \(z\), writing the resulting full-row-rank objects as \(B^\circ\) and \(p_x^\circ\), and set \(\mathcal W_x(p_x)=\{w_x\in\mathbb R_+^{|\mathcal R|}:B^\circ w_x=p_x^\circ,\ \mathbf 1^\top w_x=1\}\).

definitions.name: reduced primal--dual saddle program
definitions.construction: For every nonsingular response basis \(\beta\), set \(w_{x,\beta}=\widetilde B_\beta^{-1}\widetilde p_x\), retain \(\beta\in\mathcal B_x(p_x)\) when \(w_{x,\beta}\geq0\), and solve \(\min_{q,t}t\) subject to \(q\in\Delta_K\) and \(G_{(b,\beta),\cdot}(p_x)q\leq t\) for every \(b\in\mathcal A\) and \(\beta\in\mathcal B_x(p_x)\). Duplicate projected vertices may be retained because they do not change the feasible epigraph.

definitions.name: \mathcal K_j(p_x)
definitions.construction: \(\mathcal K_j(p_x)=\{\lambda\geq0:\mathbf 1^\top\lambda=1,\ \lambda_{b\beta}=0\text{ for }(b,\beta)\notin\mathcal S_j(p_x),\ \sum_{b,\beta}\lambda_{b\beta}[G_{(b,\beta),a}(p_x)-G_{(b,\beta),j}(p_x)]\geq0\text{ for every }a\in\mathcal A\}\).

definitions.name: coordinatewise rectangle benchmark
definitions.construction: \(\mathcal M_x^{\Box}(p_x)=\prod_{a\in\mathcal A}[L_{ax},U_{ax}]\), with \(Q_x^{\Box}(p_x)\) and \(v_x^{\Box}(p_x)\) obtained from the joint saddle definition after replacing \(\mathcal M_x(p_x)\) by \(\mathcal M_x^{\Box}(p_x)\).

definitions.name: rectangle-preservation certificates
definitions.construction: Define \(\mathcal F_x^{\mathrm{val}}(p_x)=\{q\in\Delta_K:h_{\mathcal M_x^{\Box}(p_x)}(e_b-q)\leq v_x(p_x)\ \forall b\}\), and define \(\mathcal F_x^{\mathrm{arg}}(p_x)\) to be the condition \(Q_x^*(p_x)\subseteq\mathcal F_x^{\mathrm{val}}(p_x)\).

definitions.name: \mathcal C_n(\alpha)
definitions.construction: Conditional on \(N_{xz}\), let \(I_{xzay,n}(\alpha)\) be the two-sided Clopper--Pearson interval at error \(\alpha/(2K|\mathcal X||\mathcal Z|)\) for \(N_{xzay}\) out of \(N_{xz}\), with \(I_{xzay,n}(\alpha)=[0,1]\) when \(N_{xz}=0\). Then \(\mathcal C_n(\alpha)\) is the set of collections \(p=(p_x)_{x\in\mathcal X}\) whose cells lie in all these intervals, whose rows lie in their multinomial simplices, and for which \(\mathcal W_x(p_x)\neq\varnothing\) for every \(x\).

definitions.name: \widehat{\mathcal Q}_{x,n}(\alpha)
definitions.construction: \(\widehat{\mathcal Q}_{x,n}(\alpha)=\bigcup_{p\in\mathcal C_n(\alpha)}Q_x^*(p_x)\). Compute the union by enumerating reduced primal--dual active bases, retaining the semialgebraic parameter cell on which each basis is feasible and optimal, and projecting its rational optimizer map onto \(\Delta_K\).

definitions.name: \overline R_{x,n}(\widetilde q_x;\alpha)
definitions.construction: \(\overline R_{x,n}(\widetilde q_x;\alpha)=\sup_{p\in\mathcal C_n(\alpha)}\max_{b\in\mathcal A}h_{\mathcal M_x(p_x)}(e_b-\widetilde q_x)\), augmented by the reported primal--dual solver gap when the supremum is computed numerically.

definitions.name: active-system plug-in map
definitions.construction: For active scenario rows \(\mathcal I=\mathcal I_x(p_x)\) and positive policy coordinates \(\mathcal J=\mathcal J_x(p_x)\), order \(u_x=(q_{x,\mathcal J}^*,v_x,\lambda_{\mathcal I},\eta_x)\) and set \[H_x(p_x)=\begin{bmatrix}G_{\mathcal I,\mathcal J}(p_x)&-\mathbf 1_{\mathcal I}&0&0\\0&0&G_{\mathcal I,\mathcal J}(p_x)^\top&-\mathbf 1_{\mathcal J}\\\mathbf 1_{\mathcal J}^\top&0&0&0\\0&0&\mathbf 1_{\mathcal I}^\top&0\end{bmatrix},\qquad g_x(p_x)=\begin{bmatrix}0_{\mathcal I}\\0_{\mathcal J}\\1\\1\end{bmatrix}.\] Solve \(H_x(p_x)u_x(p_x)=g_x(p_x)\), zero-pad through \(E_x(p_x)\), and define \(J_x(p_x)[h]=-E_x(p_x)H_x(p_x)^{-1}DH_x(p_x)[h]u_x(p_x)\).

definitions.name: \mathfrak P_{\kappa,\varepsilon}
definitions.construction: \(\{P_{\mathrm{obs}}\in\mathfrak P_{\mathrm{IV}}:\text{ Assumptions ass:fixed-cell-support, ass:response-basis-roster-margin, ass:unique-primal-dual-face, ass:active-system-rank, ass:primal-slack-margin, ass:reduced-cost-margin, and ass:active-weight-margin hold for every }x\in\mathcal X\}\).

definitions.name: \mathfrak H_{\mathrm{face}}
definitions.construction: Use adjacent active-basis enumeration to express the directional derivative of the graph and support functions of \(Q_x^*(p_x)\), then apply the Fang--Santos numerical delta method to those support functions and invert the resulting simultaneous inequalities.

statements.statement: For every stratum \(x\), uniformly over \(P_{\mathrm{obs}}\in\mathfrak P_{\kappa,\varepsilon}\), the feasible response-basis roster \(\mathcal B_x(p_x)\), active regret rows \(\mathcal I_x(p_x)\), and positive policy coordinates \(\mathcal J_x(p_x)\) are locally constant. The KKT vector is the unique solution of \(H_x(p_x)u_x(p_x)=g_x(p_x)\), and \(T_x:p_x\mapsto((q_x^*(p_x))^\top,v_x(p_x))^\top\) is Hadamard differentiable tangentially to the fixed-support multinomial space with derivative \(J_x(p_x)[h]=-E_x(p_x)H_x(p_x)^{-1}DH_x(p_x)[h]u_x(p_x)\). The right-hand side \(g_x(p_x)\) is constant on the face while \(H_x(p_x)\) depends on \(p_x\) through \(G_{\mathcal I_x,\mathcal J_x}(p_x)\). Within each fixed active cell, either every active facet normal is locally constant up to positive scale or the laws satisfying \(\omega_x(p_x)=0\) lie in a proper algebraic subset; at every law with \(\omega_x(p_x)>0\), no neighborhood has an epigraph description in the original \((q,t)\)-coordinates with a fixed left-hand coefficient matrix and all dependence on \(p_x\) confined to the right-hand side after redundant inequalities are removed. For every \(\delta>0\), \[\sup_{P_{\mathrm{obs}}\in\mathfrak P_{\kappa,\varepsilon}}P_{\mathrm{obs}}\left(\left\|\sqrt n\{T_x(\widehat p_x)-T_x(p_x)\}-\frac1{\sqrt n}\sum_{i=1}^nJ_x(p_x)\psi_x(O_i)\right\|>\delta\right)\longrightarrow0,\] and the law of \(\sqrt n\{T_x(\widehat p_x)-T_x(p_x)\}\) converges uniformly in bounded-Lipschitz distance to \(N(0,J_x(p_x)\Sigma_x(p_x)J_x(p_x)^\top)\).
statements.justification: The coefficient-sensitive expansion supplies regular inference for both policy weights and worst-case regret on an explicit observable margin class.
statements.gap: KlattMunkZemel2022RandomLP and LiuBuneaNilesWeed2023LPConfidence hold the constraint normals fixed and perturb right-hand sides; the categorical-instrument response bases make the active regret normals move with the estimated cell table, producing the additional \(-H^{-1}(DH)u\) term and ruling out their fixed-matrix representation on the stated class.
statements.consumer: The released Hruza et al. multicategory implementation can attach short Gaussian regions to mixed policy weights and certified regret whenever the reported basis, slack, complementarity, and moving-normal diagnostics exceed their margins.

statements.statement: For every compatible \(p_x\) and action \(j\in\mathcal A\), \(e_j\in Q_x^*(p_x)\) if and only if \(\mathcal K_j(p_x)\neq\varnothing\). Enumerating the response-fiber bases that generate \(G_x(p_x)\) turns this condition into a finite Boolean combination of weak polynomial inequalities in the observable cells \(p_{xzay}\); this is an observable necessary-and-sufficient certificate, not merely a sufficient dominance check.
statements.justification: The certificate identifies precisely when randomization has no minimax value despite three or more actions.
statements.gap: Stoye2007ManyTreatments gives an explicit spike-state solution, but no observable categorical-instrument criterion for pure optimality over a restricted joint mean polytope.
statements.consumer: Applied analysts can screen every stratum for a certified deterministic action before invoking a mixed-policy solver.

statements.statement: For every compatible \(p_x\), \(v_x^{\Box}(p_x)=v_x(p_x)\) if and only if \(\mathcal F_x^{\mathrm{val}}(p_x)\neq\varnothing\). Equality of the complete optimizer correspondences, \(Q_x^{\Box}(p_x)=Q_x^*(p_x)\), holds if and only if \(\mathcal F_x^{\mathrm{arg}}(p_x)\) holds. Both conditions admit finite observable basis certificates.
statements.justification: Value preservation and rule preservation are distinct questions, and the theorem locates their exact observable frontiers.
statements.gap: HruzaEtAl2026CategoricalPIL uses coordinatewise bounds in its loss, while SongEtAl2026CategoricalIV supplies joint restrictions; no prior theorem states when discarding those restrictions is decision-neutral.
statements.consumer: The certificate tells a user of interval-based categorical policy learning whether the existing objective is safe or must be replaced by the joint oracle.

statements.statement: Suppose \(\mathcal M_x(p_x)\) contains every Stoye spike vector \(s_a\). Then \(R_x(q,p_x)=\max_{a\in\mathcal A}\{(1-q_a)U_{ax}-\sum_{c\neq a}q_cL_{cx}\}\) for every \(q\in\Delta_K\), so \(Q_x^*(p_x)\) and \(v_x(p_x)\) equal the allocation correspondence and value in Proposition 1 of Stoye2007ManyTreatments. For \(K=2\), the formula reduces to the standard binary fractional minimax-regret rule.
statements.justification: The reduction is the required sanity check and separates genuinely joint restrictions from the classical spike geometry.
statements.gap: Stoye2007ManyTreatments assumes the spike states are available; the present statement derives his rule as the exact special case of a categorical-instrument identified polytope.
statements.consumer: Decision theorists can reuse Stoye's closed-form allocation whenever the observable spike-feasibility certificates pass.

statements.statement: The construction \(p^\dagger\) is generated by \(w^\dagger\), and the structural zeros leave exactly twenty compatible response-type columns. Its sharp projected polytope is \(\mathcal M^\dagger=\{\mu\in\mathbb R^3:0\leq\mu_0\leq3/4,\ 1/4\leq\mu_1\leq3/4,\ 1/2\leq\mu_2\leq1,\ \mu_0\leq\mu_2\}\), with vertex set \(\{(0,1/4,1/2),(0,1/4,1),(0,3/4,1/2),(0,3/4,1),(1/2,1/4,1/2),(1/2,3/4,1/2),(3/4,1/4,3/4),(3/4,1/4,1),(3/4,3/4,3/4),(3/4,3/4,1)\}\). The joint saddle has the unique solution \(q^\dagger=(0,1/4,3/4)\) and value \(3/16\), whereas the coordinatewise rectangle oracle has the unique solution \((0,0,1)\) and value \(1/4\). Thus the rectangle oracle fails at this law, changing both the deployed mixture and its worst-case regret by \(1/16\).
statements.justification: A realizable exact witness demonstrates a strict policy and regret gain from respecting cross-action feasibility.
statements.gap: HruzaEtAl2026CategoricalPIL cannot express randomized joint-polytope optimality, and a single inequality such as \(\mu_0\leq\mu_2\) alone would not establish the stated numbers; this theorem supplies the complete observable law, latent realization, facets, and vertices.
statements.consumer: The witness is a regression test for the released multicategory code and every response-type basis enumerator used in the paper.

statements.statement: Under independent sampling, for every \(P_{\mathrm{obs}}\in\mathfrak P_{\mathrm{IV}}\), \(P_{\mathrm{obs}}\{Q_x^*(p_x)\subseteq\widehat{\mathcal Q}_{x,n}(\alpha)\text{ for all }x\in\mathcal X\}\geq1-\alpha\). The active-basis algorithm computes exactly the union in the definition, including zero-count cells and laws on intersections of optimal faces; the coverage statement is finite-sample and uniform over \(\mathfrak P_{\mathrm{IV}}\).
statements.justification: Inference must cover the entire optimal correspondence, not an unstable selected optimizer.
statements.gap: SongEtAl2026CategoricalIV covers simultaneous linear counterfactual functionals and ChernozhukovHongTamer2007Sets studies criterion-minimizer sets; neither gives exact finite-sample inversion for this coefficient-varying causal saddle correspondence.
statements.consumer: A software implementation can return a certified set of all population-optimal mixtures even at face ties and with rare observed cells.

statements.statement: On the simultaneous event \(p\in\mathcal C_n(\alpha)\), every data-dependent deployed mixture \(\widetilde q_x\in\Delta_K\) satisfies \(R_x(\widetilde q_x,p_x)\leq\overline R_{x,n}(\widetilde q_x;\alpha)\) for every \(x\). Consequently, with probability at least \(1-\alpha\), all deployed-stratum inequalities hold simultaneously, including the reported numerical primal--dual gap.
statements.justification: Coverage of an optimizer set does not by itself certify the actual policy sent to deployment.
statements.gap: ClopperPearson1934Binomial supplies cellwise coverage, but the decision-level robust regret certificate and solver-error accounting are absent from categorical-instrument policy learning.
statements.consumer: A clinical or public-policy deployment can report an auditable upper bound on worst-case welfare loss for the mixture actually used.

statements.statement: For every \(P_{\mathrm{obs}}\in\mathfrak P_{\mathrm{IV}}\) and stratum \(x\), the published response-function compatibility fiber projects to \(\mathcal M_x(p_x)=\{Cw_x:w_x\in\mathcal W_x(p_x)\}\). Composing that polytope with the standard finite-scenario randomized-regret program gives \(R_x(q,p_x)=\max_{b,\beta}G_{(b,\beta),\cdot}(p_x)q\), and feasible-basis enumeration returns \(Q_x^*(p_x)\) and \(v_x(p_x)\), including tied optimal faces.
statements.justification: The lemma fixes the population optimization notation consumed by the coefficient-varying KKT and inference results.
statements.gap: SongEtAl2026CategoricalIV supplies the compatible response-law polytope and MastinJailletChin2014RandomizedRegret supplies the finite randomized-regret linear program, so their composition is treated as background rather than a new theorem-level contribution.
statements.consumer: All later certificates, the exact witness, and the moving-coefficient limit theorem use this common finite saddle representation.

statements.statement: Can \(\mathfrak H_{\mathrm{face}}\) be used to construct a computable random set whose support functions contract at the \(\sqrt n\) rate and whose coverage of \(Q_x^*(p_x)\) remains uniform along sequences approaching intersections of optimal faces, without imposing a unique optimizer or selecting one population face?
statements.justification: This is the unresolved bridge between conservative exact coverage and informative local inference at nonsmooth policy ties.
statements.gap: FangSantos2019DirectionalInference handles directionally differentiable maps, while LiuBuneaNilesWeed2023LPConfidence treats fixed-matrix LP sets; neither establishes uniform \(\sqrt n\)-rate contraction for the moving-coefficient categorical-instrument optimizer graph.
statements.consumer: The answer determines whether tie-heavy categorical-treatment applications can receive informative rather than merely valid optimizer sets.

sampling_model.design: Independent superpopulation sampling with a randomized finite-support instrument conditional on each finite covariate stratum.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: Conditional multinomial cell probabilities are empirical within \((x,z)\); finite-sample inversion uses cellwise Clopper--Pearson intervals and asymptotics use their multinomial influence vectors.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: The paper learns deterministic categorical rules by minimizing a loss formed from coordinatewise action-mean intervals and explicitly leaves randomized rules for future development.
Proposition 1 characterizes all minimax allocations when every action-specific spike state is feasible.
Theorems 2 and 3 establish local asymptotic minimaxity of an empirical-success statistical treatment rule with many point-identified treatments under an asymptotically balanced sampling design.

Theorem 5.1 gives a binary stochastic policy whose treatment probability is formed from lower and upper bounds on a conditional treatment-effect contrast and improves the deterministic worst-case-regret bound.
Theorem 1 gives necessary and sufficient inequalities for compatibility of a full categorical-instrument counterfactual distribution.
Response functions and linear programming deliver tight symbolic bounds for finite causal models.
Randomized minimax regret over a finite uncertainty set is representable as a zero-sum linear program.
Random-right-hand-side linear programs have optimizer limits whose form depends on degeneracy and the selection rule.
Auxiliary linear programs yield limits and confidence sets for optimal solutions when the constraint matrix and objective are fixed and the right-hand side is random.
Directionally differentiable maps require derivative-aware inference and generally invalidate the ordinary bootstrap when full differentiability fails.
Criterion inversion constructs confidence regions for parameter sets defined by population minimization.
Local Gaussian limit experiments characterize asymptotically minimax treatment rules when partially identified bounds shrink at the root-n scale.

tldr: The headline result is a uniform sampling law for the population randomized minimax-regret rule when categorical-instrument cell probabilities move both the active saddle coefficients and the response-fiber right-hand side. An observable nondegenerate unique-face class stabilizes every response basis and KKT face, yields the derivative \(-E H^{-1}(DH)u\), and proves that the problem is not a fixed-matrix random-right-hand-side linear program. The response-function projection and finite randomized-regret composition are background. Supporting results give pure-rule and rectangularization certificates, an exact three-action rectangle-oracle separation, finite-sample correspondence coverage, and deployed-regret certification; uniform \(\sqrt n\)-contraction at intersecting faces remains open.

project_justification.gap: Random-linear-program limit theory fixes the constraint normals, while many-treatment statistical-rule theory studies repeated-sample decisions under point identification and existing partial-identification randomization formulas use binary marginal bounds. None gives fixed-law sampling inference for a categorical-instrument population mixture whose active regret normals change with the observed multinomial table.
project_justification.niche: The missing object is an observable active-system theory that tracks changes in the response-basis roster, active regret scenarios, policy support, and KKT coefficients before applying a delta method.
project_justification.fill: The paper states a nondegenerate unique-face margin class entirely in observable basis and KKT quantities, derives the moving-coefficient derivative and a uniform asymptotic linear representation, and proves a facet-normal obstruction to any fixed-matrix right-hand-side reduction. Exact set coverage and the three-action rectangle-oracle witness remain supporting consequences.

related_work: Manski2000TreatmentChoice separates treatment choice from point identification, and Stoye2007ManyTreatments supplies the spike-state population allocation benchmark recovered by Theorem 4. Masten2023ManyTreatmentRules studies statistical treatment rules that map experimental samples into allocations and proves local asymptotic minimaxity under point identification and asymptotically balanced designs; the target here is instead the fixed-law sampling distribution of a population mixed-action optimizer under partial identification. Cui2021PartialIDDecisions, Section 5.3 and Theorem 5.1, randomizes a binary action using marginal lower and upper bounds on a treatment-effect contrast; it does not optimize over three or more actions against the joint categorical-instrument response polytope or analyze the sampling law of that optimizer. SongEtAl2026CategoricalIV supplies the sharp compatible response-law set, SachsEtAl2023SymbolicBounds supplies response-function linear programming, and MastinJailletChin2014RandomizedRegret supplies the finite saddle template, so their composition is background. HruzaEtAl2026CategoricalPIL uses a deterministic coordinatewise-interval loss; Theorem 5 gives only an exact rectangle-oracle separation for its population benchmark. BonnansShapiro2000Perturbation informs the KKT margins. KlattMunkZemel2022RandomLP and LiuBuneaNilesWeed2023LPConfidence analyze fixed coefficient matrices with random right-hand sides, whereas Theorem 1 proves that the active categorical-instrument regret normals move. FangSantos2019DirectionalInference informs the open face-intersection handle. ClopperPearson1934Binomial and ChernozhukovHongTamer2007Sets inform the supporting finite-sample set inversion. MontielOleaQiuStoye2026Asymptotics studies a local Gaussian treatment-choice experiment rather than fixed-law inference for this population optimizer.
technical_internal_limitation: The presolve evidence was independently checked computationally but is not treated as proof. For the displayed witness, response-type filtering leaves twenty compatible columns; support-direction enumeration returns the ten stated projected vertices and the facets \(0\leq\mu_0\leq3/4\), \(1/4\leq\mu_1\leq3/4\), \(1/2\leq\mu_2\leq1\), and \(\mu_0\leq\mu_2\). Independent linear programs return \(q^\dagger=(0,1/4,3/4)\), \(v=3/16\), and the rectangle solution \((0,0,1)\), \(v^{\Box}=1/4\). The proof stage must reproduce these results by exact basis certificates and repeat the check under codimension-one perturbations; any omitted optimizer or false pure-rule certificate kills the angle.
honest_scope: The categorical-instrument response representation and its composition with a finite randomized-regret linear program are background ingredients, not the contribution. Theorem 1 is confined to the observable class on which all response bases and the unique primal--dual face are separated by fixed margins. Its fixed-matrix obstruction applies at laws where the observable projective-normal diagnostic is positive; the exceptional zero set is characterized rather than assumed away. The Gaussian result excludes face intersections. The Bonferroni set remains valid there without a contraction claim; uniformly honest \(\sqrt n\)-contraction at intersecting faces is the open-ended question.
seeds: Coefficient-varying unique-face limit theory for categorical-instrument saddle programs.
Joint-polytope saddle correspondence with observable pure-rule and rectangularization if-and-only-if certificates.
Exact confidence-fiber inversion for the optimizer graph and deployed-regret certificates.
Critical instrument-strength frontier for lossless rectangularization.
Observable spike-feasibility characterization for the Stoye reduction.
Output-sensitive enumeration of projected categorical-instrument vertices.
Directional support-function inference at intersections of optimal faces.
Hausdorff control of regret distortion from coordinatewise rectangularization.

seed_details.seed: Joint-polytope saddle correspondence with pure-rule and rectangularization frontiers
seed_details.anchor: HruzaEtAl2026CategoricalPIL, Sections 2--3 and Discussion; SongEtAl2026CategoricalIV, Theorem 1 and sufficiency proof
seed_details.opportunity: Replace deterministic interval loss by the full response-fiber support function and characterize the complete mixed minimax set.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: After sharp counterfactual compatibility, keep the joint projection and introduce an outer simplex saddle problem instead of optimizing one loading or substituting marginal endpoints.
seed_details.destination_search: Searches for categorical instrumental variable randomized minimax regret and joint-polytope treatment rules found Hruza et al., Song et al., and general randomized-regret work, but no occupied target--method pair.
seed_details.red_team: Immediate from Song et al. plus a generic linear program because the identified set is already polyhedral.
seed_details.rebuttal: The objection controls theorem-level positioning: the projection-plus-saddle composition is background, while the certificates and exact witness remain supporting results for the moving-coefficient inference kernel.

literature_map: Masten (2023, Sections 2.1--2.5, Theorems 2--3) studies statistical treatment rules under point identification and balanced local experiments, not the sampling law of a partially identified population optimizer. Cui (2021, Section 5.3, Theorem 5.1) derives a binary randomized rule from marginal treatment-effect bounds, not a multicategory joint-polytope saddle or its moving-coefficient KKT map. Song et al. (2026, Theorem 1 and Section 1.2), Sachs et al. (2023), and Mastin, Jaillet, and Chin (2014) jointly supply the background response-law and finite-game construction. Hruza et al. (2026, Section 3.1 and Discussion) provide the deterministic coordinatewise-interval implementation benchmark, while the proposal claims only the displayed law's exact rectangle-oracle failure. Klatt, Munk, and Zemel (2022) and Liu, Bunea, and Niles-Weed (2023) hold the coefficient matrix fixed and perturb a right-hand side; the selected theorem instead derives a uniform limit when response-basis regret normals move with the observable cells. Bonnans and Shapiro (2000) supply general strong-regularity ingredients, Fang and Santos (2019) supplies directional inference tools for the open face-intersection problem, and Montiel Olea, Qiu, and Stoye (2026) studies a distinct local Gaussian treatment-choice experiment.
novelty_justification: The theorem-level delta is the observable moving-coefficient KKT result: uniform response-basis and active-face stability, the explicit derivative \(-E H^{-1}(DH)u\), a projective-normal obstruction to a fixed-matrix right-hand-side representation, and a uniform asymptotic linear and Gaussian law for the population mixed policy and regret. The response-polytope saddle composition is background; the pure-rule, rectangle-frontier, exact witness, and finite-sample coverage results support the inference kernel.
message: Recentered the proposal on the moving-coefficient KKT limit theorem, demoted the generic saddle composition, repaired the rectangle-oracle claim, added Masten (2023) and Cui (2021), and passed proposal-gate, symbol, dependency, JSON, and LaTeX checks.

literature_checklist.author: Masten
literature_checklist.one_line: Sections 2.1–2.5 and Theorems 2–3 concern repeated-sample statistical rules with many point-identified treatments, not inference for a population mixed optimizer under partial identification.

literature_checklist.author: Cui
literature_checklist.one_line: Section 5.3 and Theorem 5.1 derive a binary stochastic policy from marginal treatment-effect bounds rather than a multicategory joint response polytope.

literature_checklist.author: Klatt, Munk, and Zemel
literature_checklist.one_line: Optimizer limits depend on degeneracy and selection in fixed-matrix random-right-hand-side linear programs.

literature_checklist.author: Liu, Bunea, and Niles-Weed
literature_checklist.one_line: Auxiliary linear programs characterize unique and nonunique optimizer limits when only the right-hand side is random.
